steps.message:
# Ship is damaged when performing the action shown in the recording

### What happens
`recording.mp4` shows a ship performing an action at a station. The action does not
go the way it is set up to go, and the ship does not come out of it unharmed.
The collision outlines of the ship and the pad already overlap while the ship sits still, although the video shows it resting clear of the pad. A ship that really lands on a pad must still be caught by it, and the ship's overall shape must stay as it is.

### Expected
Performing the action shown in the recording must not damage the ship at all, at the spot shown in
the video or at any other equivalent spot of the same station. The hull-integrity readout stays at
100% for the whole action.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

You can inspect the video frame by frame with `ffmpeg` (installed in the image), e.g. extracting
still frames at specific timestamps to look closely at the HUD and the ship.

Inspect the attached file before making changes. The video describes observable behavior; it does
not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

steps.message:
I fixed the bug in the station's pad data, but I haven't checked it in the running game. I only measured the model geometry, and I haven't built the game or replayed the take-off.

**What the video shows:** the ship rests on a ground-station pad and lifts off, and hull integrity drops from 100% to 99% just as it leaves the pad.

**Cause:** in `data/models/stations/new_ground/new_ground_landing.dae`, the invisible collision surfaces of the pads sat higher than the visible pad tops and the landing points:

| | Height (z) |
|---|---|
| Visible pad top, all 6 pads (`new_ground_hi.dae`) | 72.582 |
| Landing point the ship is placed on, all 6 pads | 72.582 |
| Pad 1 collision surface | 73.308 (0.73 m too high) |
| Pads 2–6 collision surfaces | ~72.838 (0.26 m too high) |

So a landed ship looked clear of the pad but was really sunk into its collision surface. Once the ship starts flying away, the pad no longer counts it as docked. Any contact with the pad from that point is treated as a crash, so the overlap at liftoff cost hull.

**Fix:** I moved all six pad collision surfaces down to z=72.582, level with the visible pad and the landing points. This also covers the other pads ("equivalent spots") on the same station. That's the only change, six lines in one file.
- **Landing still works:** the pads still have their collision surfaces, now at the height of the visible pad, so a ship landing is still caught.
